title: Executive Order 14110 on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI
summary: Comprehensive AI executive order establishing safety requirements, reporting thresholds and agency directives. Required developers of dual-use foundation models to share safety test results with the federal government. Rescinded on 2025-01-20 and replaced by Executive Order 14179.

title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
summary: Voluntary framework for managing AI risks throughout the AI lifecycle. Organized around four core functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage.
key_provisions: Four core functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage)

title: OMB Memorandum M-24-10: AI Governance
summary: Required federal agencies to implement AI governance structures, designate Chief AI Officers and apply safeguards to rights-impacting and safety-impacting AI. Superseded in April 2025 by OMB M-25-21.

title: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights
summary: Non-binding framework identifying five principles for automated systems: safe and effective systems, algorithmic discrimination protections, data privacy, notice and explanation, and human alternatives. Published under the previous administration and no longer hosted on the current White House site.

title: SEC AI-Related Disclosure Guidance
summary: Commission statements and enforcement posture on AI-related disclosure, including 'AI washing' in public company filings. This entry describes a supervisory posture rather than a single discrete issuance and needs confirmation against a specific SEC document.

title: FTC AI and Algorithm Enforcement
summary: FTC enforcement focus on AI-related unfair and deceptive practices, including algorithmic discrimination and AI-enabled fraud.
key_provisions: Section 5 unfairness authority for AI harms

title: DoD Data, Analytics and AI Adoption Strategy
summary: Strategy for accelerating DoD adoption of AI capabilities while maintaining ethical principles and safety standards.

title: Commerce Department AI Export Controls
summary: Export controls on advanced AI chips and related technology to certain foreign countries, particularly China.

title: Executive Order 14179: Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence
summary: Revoked Executive Order 14110 and reoriented federal AI policy toward promoting innovation and American AI leadership, directing agencies to identify and revise policies that act as barriers to AI development.
key_provisions: Directs an action plan to sustain American AI leadership
Requires agency review of policies inconsistent with the new policy
Removes the prior safety-reporting and compute-threshold framework

title: Executive Order 14365: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
summary: Directs federal agencies to pursue a uniform national AI policy and to challenge state AI laws considered onerous. An executive order cannot itself preempt state law, and as of September 2026 no state AI law has been held preempted.
key_provisions: Establishes a Department of Justice AI Litigation Task Force
Directs Commerce to evaluate burdensome state AI laws
Directs an FTC policy statement and an FCC disclosure proceeding
Ties eligibility for some federal broadband funds to state AI policy
Expressly excludes state child-safety, compute infrastructure and state procurement laws

title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI
summary: Replaced M-24-10 as the governing policy for federal agency use of AI, retaining Chief AI Officers and AI use case inventories while shifting emphasis toward adoption and removing some of the prior memo's risk-management requirements.
key_provisions: Retains annual AI use case inventories
Introduces a high-impact AI category with minimum practices
